Load Balancer (NGINX+) — Changes Needed to Onboard New RHEL9 Servers

 

 

The new RHEL9 servers listed above need to be added to the existing NGINX+ load balancer upstream pools. The current RHEL7 servers will remain in place — no decommissioning.

Current LB Configuration (elktest.omf.cloud)

All farms are hosted on the test NGINX+ cluster (evnginxplust05/06.corp.fin), configured via Ansible group vars at group_vars/test/test.yml. All use TLS 1.2, elktest.omf.cloud certs, and 64k upstream zones.

Action Items

  1. DNS/Infoblox — Register all new RHEL9 hostnames (evelkwkn01-03test, evelklsn01-02, evelkftn01-02) with their IPs so NGINX can resolve them.

  2. Update Ansible group vars — Add the new server hostnames to the appropriate upstream blocks in group_vars/test/test.yml in the evdcigl.corp.fin/shared-datacomm/nginx repo.

  3. Health check ports — Ensure the correct backend ports are open and responding on the new servers before adding: Elasticsearch (9200), Kibana (5601), Logstash (5044, 5043, 8443, 5041, 5046).

  4. TLS certs — Stage elktest.omf.cloud certificates on the new RHEL9 servers for SSL passthrough/termination.

  5. Zone memory — Current upstream zones are 64k each. With additional upstream members, consider increasing proactively. Prod already hit a zone memory issue (see NETENG-438: Increase zone memory for logstash-beats.elk.omf.cloud server farm from 128k to 1mDonePreview — had to increase from 128k to 1m for logstash-beats.elk.omf.cloud).

  6. Coordinate with NCE — Technical owner for all elktest farms is Cody Moore. He will need to approve/make the Ansible changes and reload the NGINX config.

Note: The test NGINX+ cluster (evnginxplust05/06) is currently at capacity (63 farms). No new farms are needed - only upstream additions to existing farms - so this should not be a blocker.
